walkthroughs.body_html:
Abstract Data Structures — a core area of Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Abstract Data Structures brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Abstract Data Structures.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm was published in:

options: FIFO
LIFO
Round robin
Priority

mcqs.q: What is the scope of a local variable?
options: Accessible only within the function/block where it is declared.
The computer crashes.
Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
Accessible everywhere in the program.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: They produce different programming languages.
A compiler translates the whole program first; an interpreter executes line by line.
Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
A compiler is a person, an interpreter is software.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.
The computer crashes.
